summary: ORBIT CARE is an deep-space health monitoring and clinical triage web application designed for long-duration missions. The platform continuously tracks crew biometrics and Environmental Control and Life Support Systems (ECLSS) to instantly detect anomalies. It resolves 20-minute communication delays by autonomously executing life-support actions and assigning targeted NASA HRP countermeasure missions. The system provides astronauts with step-by-step emergency checklists for split-second crisis management offline. Complete diagnostic reports are automatically buffered and queued for transmission to ground control once communication windows reopen.
details: We built ORBIT CARE, a web application that monitors astronaut health and spacecraft life support systems during deep-space missions. The system works by tracking vital signs and cabin conditions in real time to detect any sudden issues, like high carbon dioxide levels or low oxygen, and then it automatically triggers fixes and gives the crew simple step-by-step checklists to follow. The main benefit is that astronauts do not have to wait up to twenty minutes for instructions from Earth during an emergency, which makes deep-space travel much safer and keeps the crew healthy using daily exercise and wellness missions. We developed this website using HTML, CSS, Tailwind, and JavaScript to create a clean and responsive dashboard. Our project is creative because instead of making a complicated screen with too much data, we designed a fast triage system that links real NASA health risks directly to practical actions and saves reports to send to Earth whenever the connection comes back. When building it, our team focused on keeping the interface very easy to read under stress, making sure it works completely offline, and following real NASA safety standards.
